svg.aria-label: CleanDocs AI: a single file, then a ZIP, move step by step through upload, checksum, validate, archive, SQS, normalize, extract, enrich, chunk, embed and vectorize; failures go to the DLQ
svg.text: Document ingestion and indexing, built on AWS

g.text: Upload anything
PDF, scans, Word, Excel, text, ZIP
Reads scans (OCR)
Amazon Textract, confidence tracked
Labels itself
LLM doc type, tags, summary, PII flag
Search-ready chunks
Citations: page, section, owner, date
Resilient microservices
16 services, SQS + DLQ, retries, audit trail

svg.text: From upload to searchable index, step by step
one file, then a ZIP, then what happens when a step fails

g.text: Upload
Upload service stores the untouched original in S3
Owner and Idempotency-Key are recorded, so a retry is safe
Starts the Step Functions ingestion workflow
Checksum
SHA-256 is computed and verified by S3 on write
Exact duplicates are detected: skip, link or reprocess
The original is immutable: written once, never overwritten
Validate
File type is read from the content (magic bytes), not the extension
Size, page and image-pixel limits are enforced
Bad files are rejected early and safely
Archive
Not a ZIP, so the file passes straight through
ZIP uploads take a different route (see the next scene)
Each file is tracked as its own document
SQS
The file waits in the SQS queue
A dispatcher feeds one file at a time through the DynamoDB gate
Failed steps retry, then the message moves to the DLQ
Normalize
PDF, Word, Excel, CSV and images become uniform page/block JSON
Cleaning fixes whitespace, hyphenation and control characters
Pages that need OCR are marked
Extract
Real text is kept; scanned pages go to Amazon Textract (OCR)
OCR confidence is stored; a monthly page cap bounds the spend
Rule-based title, type guess, dates and keywords are added
Enrich
One Nova Micro call returns type, tags, summary, language, date, PII flag
The answer is validated against a closed vocabulary (injection-safe)
Soft stage: it can never fail a document
Chunk
Layout-aware split: headings, tables with header rows, sentence-aware paragraphs
Overlap plus locators (page, section, sheet) for citations
Chunk ids come from the text hash, so re-ingest creates no duplicates
Embed
Chunk file plus a metadata sidecar are written for Bedrock
owner, doc_type, tags, date, language become search filters
A document becomes visible only when it is complete
Vectorize
A Bedrock ingestion job embeds the chunks with Titan Text V2
Vectors are stored in S3 Vectors (serverless, no idle cost)
Reconciliation re-checks S3 and the Knowledge Base before COMPLETED
ZIP
One ZIP upload
The whole ZIP is stored once as the untouched original
Checksum and validation run on the ZIP itself, once
Next: Archive opens it
Archive opens the ZIP
Zip-bomb limits and path checks run before anything is extracted
Every entry becomes its own document with its own status
All children inherit the owner of the upload
3 files from the ZIP, one by one
Now at step 5, SQS: The file waits in the SQS queue
Same steps as the single file: each gets its own chunks, labels and status
The SQS gate feeds them through one at a time, so cost and memory stay small
3 files from the ZIP, one by one
Now at step 6, Normalize: PDF, Word, Excel, CSV and images become uniform page/block JSON
Same steps as the single file: each gets its own chunks, labels and status
The SQS gate feeds them through one at a time, so cost and memory stay small

Now at step 7, Extract: Real text is kept; scanned pages go to Amazon Textract (OCR)
Same steps as the single file: each gets its own chunks, labels and status
The SQS gate feeds them through one at a time, so cost and memory stay small

The SQS gate feeds them through one at a time, so cost and memory stay small
3 files from the ZIP, one by one
Now at step 9, Chunk: Layout-aware split: headings, tables with header rows, sentence-aware paragraphs
Same steps as the single file: each gets its own chunks, labels and status
The SQS gate feeds them through one at a time, so cost and memory stay small
3 files from the ZIP, one by one
Now at step 10, Embed: Chunk file plus a metadata sidecar are written for Bedrock
Same steps as the single file: each gets its own chunks, labels and status
The SQS gate feeds them through one at a time, so cost and memory stay small
3 files from the ZIP, one by one
Now at step 11, Vectorize: A Bedrock ingestion job embeds the chunks with Titan Text V2
Same steps as the single file: each gets its own chunks, labels and status
The SQS gate feeds them through one at a time, so cost and memory stay small
When a step fails: SQS retries, then the DLQ
The queue retries the step automatically with back-off
After the last retry the message moves to the DLQ and is kept, not lost
Fix the cause, then replay the file from the DLQ: nothing disappears silently
